payload.selection_rationale:
One proposal (practice). It is selected as the core because it matches the tree as it stands, not because it reads well. The survey measured the slice as unbuilt. Rules 2 and 4 (.taad/fitness.yaml:746-764 and :774-791) still carry their SL-056 patterns. Five risk spikes ran against the real engine and all five came back go. Spike 1's union of patterns fires on 35 of 35 planted lines in Store, the Core root and Scanning, with 0 false hits and 0 hits on the real tree, and parity, RuleCases and the harness are unchanged. Spike 2 showed the R2-m4 two-line minimum alone makes the repro pass. Spike 3 measured the separate Attributes entry and found the `(?![=>])` lookahead. Spike 4 measured the using-static, method-group and Zw spellings, and spike 5 measured FileSystemEnumera(ble|tor).

The design stays inside the project's own rule system: settled entries in fitness.yaml, settled-only plant rows in plants.json, and the parity, RuleCases and harness checks. It adds no analyzer, and the practice designer flagged RS0030 as over-built for a gap of two rules. Every change is yaml lines and JSON rows, so it is cheap to reverse.

The practice designer also raised over_engineering_flag against their own union and named the trimmed version. That stays on the record as a taste disagreement for review. I kept the union because it was measured go at the same cost, and lesson #225 says these rules under-fence when they name one member.

Composer changes, each checked against the tree:
- Rule 4's using-static pattern now covers Enumerate* as well as Get*. Grep finds no `(Get|Enumerate)(Files|Directories|FileSystemEntries)` and no `using static` anywhere in src/FsAnalyser.Core, so the tree stays clean.
- The new entry is declared in architecture_rules, so the engine appends it. The build does not also write it by hand, which avoids a duplicate.
- Three plant rows are added: an Enumerate* using-static row, and two rows in a Scanning file that is not excepted.
- Each case's check runs the harness with `--only`, which harness.py:708 supports, so no run has to cover the whole scenario.

components.name: Rule 2 widened in place
components.responsibility: Fences every Win32, NT and .NET writer of a file-system time or attribute in src/FsAnalyser.Core/**/*.cs outside Native/Kernel32.cs and Scanning/SynchronousIoCancel.cs. The name, files and except_files do not change. The must_not_match list becomes exactly 11 contiguous single-quoted (?m) lines, with no blank, comment or double-quoted line between them: '\bSetFileInformationByHandle\b'; '\bSetFileTime\b'; '\b(Nt|Zw)SetInformationFile\b' (replaces the Nt-only line, which it contains); '\bSetFileAttributes\w*'; '\b(File|Directory)\.Set(LastAccess|LastWrite|Creation)Time' (kept for method groups); '\bSet(LastAccess|LastWrite|Creation)Time(Utc)?\s*\(' (new, for using static); '\.(LastAccess|LastWrite|Creation)Time(Utc)?\s*=(?!=)' (kept); '\bFile\.SetAttributes\b' (new, R2-m4: the qualified form and the method group); '\bSetAttributes\s*\(' (new, for using static); '\bIsReadOnly\s*=(?![=>])' (new, with spike 3's lookahead so `IsReadOnly => false` stays quiet); '\bFile\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b' (new and not run by any spike; plant S63 must prove it).
components.key_interactions: Read by taad3.fitness (whole-file finditer, case-sensitive, comments blanked because the entry has no including_comments) and by the repro's Read-YamlPatterns (per-line .NET Regex, contiguous single-quoted lines only). The entry's name must not change, because the repro header lookup and plants.json key on it. Once during the build, run [IO.File]/[IO.Directory]/[IO.FileInfo]/[IO.FileSystemInfo] GetMethods() in pwsh and list every Set*, set_*, Encrypt and Decrypt member. Any member the list shows that no pattern names is a missing pattern, not a residual (lesson #436).

components.name: Rule 4 widened in place
components.responsibility: Fences every directory listing in src/FsAnalyser.Core/**/*.cs outside Scanning/DirectoryReader.cs and Native/Kernel32.cs. The name, files and except_files do not change. The list becomes exactly 7 contiguous single-quoted (?m) lines: '\bFindFirstFile\w*'; '\b(Nt|Zw)QueryDirectoryFile\w*' (replaces the Nt-only line); '\bFile\w*Directory(Restart)?Info\b'; '\bDirectory\.(Enumerate\w*|GetFiles|GetDirectories|GetFileSystemEntries)\b' (kept); '\.(GetFiles|GetDirectories|GetFileSystemInfos|Enumerate(Files|Directories|FileSystemInfos))\b' (replaces the `\s*\(` instance pattern; it contains the old one and adds GetFiles, GetDirectories and method groups); '\b(Get|Enumerate)(Files|Directories|FileSystemEntries)\s*\(' (new, for using static Directory; widened by the composer from spike 4's Get-only form and not run by a spike, so plant S76 must prove it); '\bFileSystemEnumera(ble|tor)\b' (replaces FileSystemEnumerable).
components.key_interactions: Same readers as rule 2. A line such as `Directory.GetFiles(p)` now hits up to three patterns of the same rule, so it counts as up to three violations. Every gate tests only for more than zero (spike 2 recorded this), so no verdict changes.

components.name: New settled entry: the FileSystemInfo.Attributes setter
components.responsibility: 'Core sets no file attributes through a FileSystemInfo.Attributes write' covers src/FsAnalyser.Core/**/*.cs with the single pattern '(?m)\.Attributes\s*[|&^]?=(?!=)'. Its except_files are Scanning/DirectoryReader.cs, Native/Kernel32.cs and Scanning/SynchronousIoCancel.cs, and it has no including_comments. It is declared in this design's architecture_rules, so the engine appends it under a '# settled by SL-104' marker. The build checks that it appears exactly once with that exact name and those fields. The build does not write a second copy, does not move it above the first marker, does not twin it and does not add including_comments. If the engine has not appended it, the build writes it once, by hand, directly after rule 4's except_files under its own '# settled by SL-104' marker.
components.key_interactions: Increases the settled count from 69 to 70 and the Fitness rule count from 91 to 92. Spike 3 measured parity AGREE, RuleCases C-001..C-005 unchanged and the harness clean baseline CLEAN at 92. DirectoryReader.cs:181 (`entry.Attributes = Read<uint>(...)`) matches the pattern, and only except_files keeps it quiet.

components.name: Because-texts made true
components.responsibility: Rule 2's because-text drops the sentence 'So every way to write a time or an attribute is fenced, not one API name' (fitness.yaml:758). In its place it names what is fenced: the Win32 and NT setters (Nt/Zw), SetFileAttributes*, the File and Directory Set*Time statics whether qualified, taken as a method group or called through using static, the FileSystemInfo time setters, File.SetAttributes whether qualified or through using static, the IsReadOnly setter and File.Encrypt/Decrypt. It says the Attributes property setter has its own entry because DirectoryReader.cs writes a struct field of that name, and it cites SL-104/O-031. It also names what a text rule does not see, and says review holds those: object initializers ({ Attributes = ..., LastWriteTime = ... }), reflection, a delegate made from a using-static method group, and Encrypt/Decrypt through using static. Rule 4's text gains a sentence naming the DirectoryInfo instance listings (called or taken as a method group), the Directory statics through using static, and FileSystemEnumerator<T>. Both stay single-quoted folded scalars, with '' for an apostrophe. Everything after 'The declaration lives in Native/Kernel32.cs' in rule 2 stays as it is.
components.key_interactions: fitness.py skips the rules file itself, so this prose cannot trip any rule. The repro stops reading at the `    because:` line, which is not a `- '...'` line.

key_decisions.decision: Keep the regex text rules in .taad/fitness.yaml. This slice adopts neither Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.BannedApiAnalyzers (RS0030) nor an AST check.
key_decisions.rationale: The project's rule system is fitness.yaml with xUnit twins, checked by parity, RuleCases and the harness. RS0030 would add an analyzer, a BannedSymbols file per project, and pragmas in the excepted files: a second rule system for a gap of two rules. The practice designer flagged it as over-built. The alias classes it would close are filed for a later slice (lessons #400, #439).

key_decisions.decision: Use spike 1's measured union rather than the R2-m4 two-line minimum.
key_decisions.rationale: The two lines alone make the repro pass (spike 2). The investigation, however, planted 15 more spellings that escape, and lesson #225 says these rules under-fence when they name one member. The union was measured go on every guard and costs only yaml lines and plant rows. The trimmed version is recorded as a taste disagreement, so review can choose it.

key_decisions.decision: Widen in place. Where a new pattern contains an old one, replace the old one rather than adding beside it: (Nt|Zw)SetInformationFile, (Nt|Zw)QueryDirectoryFile, FileSystemEnumera(ble|tor), and the `\b`-terminated instance list. Rule 2 ends with 11 patterns and rule 4 with 7.
key_decisions.rationale: Nothing asserts the pattern count of either rule. A grep of the tree finds them read only by the repro, which prints the count and does not assert it. Each replacement matches everything the old pattern matched: wherever `\s*\(` followed the member name, the next character is not a word character, so `\b` holds there too.

key_decisions.decision: Put the FileSystemInfo.Attributes setter in a new settled entry that excepts DirectoryReader.cs. Declare that entry in architecture_rules so the engine appends it, and have the build check it exists once rather than writing it by hand.
key_decisions.rationale: except_files applies to a whole entry (Rule.covers). Excepting DirectoryReader from rule 2 would unfence the time setters in the listing code itself, and a narrower right-hand-side pattern misses `fi.Attributes = attrs;`. Spike 3 measured this entry go. Declaring it and also hand-writing it would produce two entries with one name. The engine-appended placement is honest, because only the first '# settled by' marker matters to rules-parity and RuleCases.

key_decisions.decision: The IsReadOnly pattern uses the lookahead `(?![=>])`, not the investigation's `(?!=)`.
key_decisions.rationale: Spike 3 measured `(?!=)` firing on `public bool IsReadOnly => false;`.

Both change the file's encrypted attribute, so they belong to the family rule 2's because-text names, and spike 1 recorded both as still escaping. A grep finds neither in src/FsAnalyser.Core. No spike ran them, so plant S63 and the clean baseline prove them at build.

key_decisions.decision: Widen rule 4's using-static pattern from Get* to `\b(Get|Enumerate)(Files|Directories|FileSystemEntries)\s*\(`.
key_decisions.rationale: Spike 4's Get-only form leaves `using static System.IO.Directory; ... EnumerateFiles(p)` unfenced, which is exactly the one-member under-fencing lesson #225 warns about. A grep of src/FsAnalyser.Core finds no such call, so the tree stays clean. This is a composer addition and unmeasured, so plant S76 proves it.

key_decisions.decision: Rules 2 and 4 and the new entry stay settled, with no xUnit twin.
key_decisions.rationale: Lesson #313: settled entries need no twin. Twinning would move the facts, twinned-entry and pattern counts that RuleCases and SettledCountProbe consume (#85, #158), which is a separate, larger change, filed for later.

key_decisions.decision: Prove the widened family with settled-only plant rows in new files: in Store/, at the Core root to show `**/` reaches zero levels, and in a Scanning file that is not excepted. The repro is left as written.
key_decisions.rationale: The repro is the acceptance test the engine ran. plants.json is the project's engine-level record (#330), and a new-file row owns every hit in its file, so an extra rule firing shows up as a STRAY-HIT rather than hiding.

key_decisions.decision: Rewrite rule 2's and rule 4's because-texts so they claim only what a regex can see, and name the residuals.
key_decisions.rationale: 'So every way to write a time or an attribute is fenced' (fitness.yaml:758) was false at SL-056 and stays false after any text widening: object initializers, reflection and using-static delegates escape. A rule whose stated reason overclaims is how O-031 went unnoticed.

proposals.note: The only proposal. Taken whole: the spike-1 union, spike 3's lookahead, the separate Attributes entry, the rewritten because-texts, plant rows S58-S75 and the unchanged repro. The composer changed four things: (1) the new entry goes in architecture_rules and the engine appends it, rather than the build inserting it after rule 4, so there is no duplicate; (2) rule 4's using-static pattern is widened to (Get|Enumerate); (3) rows S76-S78 are added (the using-static Enumerate row, and Scanning-file fire rows for rule 4 and the new entry); (4) each case's check runs the harness with --only <ids>. The practice designer raised over_engineering_flag against their own union and named the trimmed alternative, which is recorded under taste_disagreements.

payload.coherence_check:
There was one proposal, so there was no composition to check, and nothing in this design has yet been disagreed with by anyone. Review should argue with it first, starting with the practice designer's own over_engineering_flag: the union of patterns against the R2-m4 two-line minimum.

I did check the composer's own changes against the proposal and against the tree.

(1) The new entry. The proposal had the build insert it after rule 4. This design declares it in architecture_rules, and the engine appends declared rules as settled entries. Keeping both would put two entries with one name in fitness.yaml, so the build keeps neither path in parallel: it verifies one copy, and writes one by hand only if the engine did not. Position does not matter, because rules-parity (markerAt, rules-parity.ps1:387-391) and RuleCases look only at the first '# settled by' marker.

(2) Rules 2 and 4 are deliberately NOT declared in architecture_rules. Declaring them would make the engine append second settled entries under new names. That would split each family across two entries and make every plant fire two rules. They are widened in place instead.

(3) The repro reads contiguous single-quoted `- '...'` lines. Every new pattern is single-quoted with (?m), and no blank or comment line goes inside either list.

(4) Each replacement pattern contains the one it replaces, so controls W10-W12 and L09-L11 still fire. I checked every new pattern by hand against the quiet rows W20, W21, L20 and L21 (GetAttributes, GetLastWriteTimeUtc, GetFileName, Exists) and found no hit. `GetFilesCount(` and `SetAttributesFromEntry(` stay quiet too.

(5) The new entry excepts DirectoryReader.cs without weakening rule 2, which still fences every other writer in DirectoryReader. ScanStore.cs:229 (`page.Attributes[i] = ...`) and :409 (no leading dot) do not match the dotted pattern.

(6) Plant texts avoid every token another rule fences over Store or Core: Scanner, DirectoryReader, SizeProbe and TopLevelTracker (Store rule); ScanStore; (Library|Dll)Import, which is matched in comments too; the PathOpens entry-point names; the 1920-retry flag; and absolute user paths in notes. The Zw call spellings are not among PathOpensGoOnlyThroughTheGuardedOpen's names.

(7) A `Directory.GetFiles(` line now counts up to three violations of one rule. Every gate tests only for more than zero, so this is recorded rather than designed around.

No workaround setting applies. Nothing here steps around a defect outside the project: this fixes the project's own rules, so KnownWorkarounds is untouched.

architecture_rules.name: Core sets no file attributes through a FileSystemInfo.Attributes write
architecture_rules.because: Assigning a FileSystemInfo's Attributes (=, |=, &=, ^=) writes the file's attributes to disk through the same BCL path as File.SetAttributes. Criterion 6 forbids the scan changing file metadata outside the one listing-handle call in SynchronousIoCancel (rule 'only the directory-listing open path may write a file-system timestamp', review M8, SL-104/O-031). A second writer there would change what a person's tools show and no test would notice. This is a separate entry only because except_files covers a whole entry, and DirectoryReader.cs:181 assigns a listing struct's field of the same name, which writes nothing to disk. An object initializer { Attributes = ... } has no dot and is not caught; review holds it.

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Static-analysis deny-lists in CI (Roslyn BannedApiAnalyzers, Semgrep/grep rules)
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: Fence the API family, not one name. Match the member name independently of its receiver, so qualified, using-static and method-group spellings all fire. Pin each read-only look-alike as a must-stay-quiet row, and write down the false-negative classes the matcher cannot see instead of claiming full coverage.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: Text deny-lists that hold up in practice share three habits: the list covers the sibling family, each spelling has a fire row and a quiet row in a corpus, and the docs say what grep cannot see. SL-056's rules broke all three: one name per family, no plant row for rule 2, and a because-text claiming 'every way'. A symbol-based analyzer would close the alias class but is a larger change than this slice, so it is filed for later.

prior_art.pattern: File.SetAttributes and File.SetLastWriteTime sit side by side as File statics that write file metadata. A fence on one is incomplete without the other.
Directory.GetFiles is a directory listing served by NtQueryDirectoryFile in .NET 10, so GetFiles belongs in the same listing fence as EnumerateFiles.
FileSystemEnumerable/FileSystemEnumerator are the enumeration primitives under the Directory/DirectoryInfo listing methods, so a listing fence must name both types.
GetFiles and EnumerateFiles differ only in eager versus lazy return, so a deny-list naming one but not the other leaves the same listing open.
Symbol-based API bans by documentation-comment ID (RS0030) see using-static calls, method groups and aliases that text rules miss. Considered and not adopted here.
Grep/Semgrep-style CI deny-lists keep a fire/quiet corpus per rule and document their structural false-negative classes.
prior_art.where: Semgrep rule-testing conventions; grep-based CI lint checks

taste_disagreements: Scope: spike 1's union (rule 2 at 11 patterns, rule 4 at 7, a new entry, 21 plant rows) against the R2-m4 two-line minimum, which alone closes the repro (spike 2). The practice designer raised over_engineering_flag against their own union. The trimmed version keeps `\bFile\.SetAttributes\b`, GetFiles|GetDirectories in the instance pattern, the because-text fix and rows S58, S64 and S65, and drops everything else.

Placement of the new entry: the engine appends it at the end of the file under '# settled by SL-104' (this design), or it is hand-inserted after rule 4 so the three sibling fences read together (the proposal). Only the first marker matters to any tool.

The Attributes setter in a separate entry that excepts DirectoryReader.cs, against a narrower right-hand-side pattern (one that requires FileAttributes) inside rule 2. The narrower pattern misses `fi.Attributes = attrs;`.
Rewriting the because-texts to list what is fenced and what escapes, against simply deleting the 'every way' sentence.
